first.rationale: Current state shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ), while competitive pressure is hitting price-sensitive SMB. Memory 91 (in-product activation messaging) and memory 86 (onboarding shortening) are most directly relevant to the activation decline. I'm verifying these two to confirm their effect sizes and implementation details. Activation messaging is the preferred lever because: (1) it addresses the steepest immediate problem (6% activation drop), (2) memory_91 showed measurable week-one engagement lift, (3) it doesn't require product friction or pricing concessions that could harm long-term qualified revenue, (4) it can be deployed quickly and reverted if ineffective. This avoids promotional_pricing (memory_73 has pooling ambiguity and erodes margin on the segment most sensitive to competitor pricing) and referral_incentive (memory_57 is proven for retention but doesn't address activation decay). Onboarding simplification (memory_31) is valid but secondary—activation messaging targets the problem more directly. Enterprise_sales_assist requires confidence in sales capacity and longer cycle validation. Standard_experiment scale allows reasonable statistical power while preserving the option to iterate or pivot if results are weak.
